output.summary:
I'm abandoning this change: raising the threshold from 64 to 256 rows built fine, but no template got reliably faster. The change itself was one line: CachingPhysicalOperator::CACHE_THRESHOLD went from 64 to STANDARD_VECTOR_SIZE/8 (256) in physical_operator.hpp. Bench results:
- Full bench run 1: geomean -0.8%.
- Full bench run 2: geomean -1.3%.
- Rerun of q02/q04/q05/q08/q19: geomean +1.8%.
- Rerun of q05/q08/q17: geomean +0.8%.
Templates flip sign from run to run: q04 went -8.5% then +11.2% then +3.8%; q05 went +5.8%, -6.3%, -6.3%, then +3.2%; q08 went -8.2%, +11.1%, -4.1%, then +0.5%; q17 went -9.7% then -1.1%. That is noise. The q07 profile explains why. The operators above the selective joins and the n1/n2 OR FILTER (FILTER, projections, HASH_GROUP_BY) only see about 117K rows and take about 0.01s in total. Nearly all of the 0.45s is the lineitem/orders scans and the big HJ probe, and those were already densified at the scan level by E0040. So no per-chunk cost is left to recover. I did not do the optional DataChunk swap in Execute, and I did not measure 128 separately, because 256 already showed no signal.
output.generality: This would apply to pipelines where a hash join, filter or cross product outputs 65-255 rows per chunk and a costly operator sits above it. On the visible star/snowflake joins, the sparse join outputs feed only cheap operators, so it gains nothing measurable there.
output.notes: Dead end: coalescing operator outputs is not the bottleneck once scan outputs are coalesced (E0040). Only revisit it if a profile shows a heavy operator (big HJ probe or aggregate) sitting directly on a sparse join or filter output with about 100-250 rows per chunk. The noise band for the quick bench on these templates is about ±10% per template, so judge by repeated runs.
